reading: The Leonid meteor shower is expected to be visible across the UK during November.
The shower continues until 30 November and is expected to reach its peak on the night of 17 November.
Viewers could spot as many as 10 to 15 meteors in an hour.
As the comet Tempel-Tuttle travels around the Sun, it leaves behind a trail of dust particles.
These particles enter the layer of air around Earth at speeds of up to 71 kilometres per second, producing streaks of light.
Experts recommend finding a safe, dark place away from light pollution, which is unwanted light from sources such as street lights.
You can see the meteors with the naked eye, so you do not need binoculars or a telescope.
Allow about 20 to 30 minutes for your eyes to adjust to the dark so that you have a better chance of spotting the meteors.
An open area gives you a wide view of the night sky.
Although the forecast calls for dry weather much of the time, clouds may still block the view in many areas.
Fog could also form in places where the sky stays clear for a while, making the meteors harder to see.
Anyone who misses the meteors this weekend may have better viewing conditions near the peak in mid-November.
Near the peak, the Moon will be below the horizon around midnight, so its light is less likely to spoil the view.

vocabulary.definition: The time when the meteor shower is most active.
To notice or see something, especially when it is hard to see.
A line of material left behind as something moves.
Long, narrow lines, here made of light.
Using your eyes without equipment such as binoculars or a telescope.
To get used to a change, such as going from a bright place to a dark one.
Says that a particular kind of weather is expected.
To get in the way so that someone cannot see what they are trying to look at.
Lower than the line where the sky seems to meet the land or sea.

entries.ja: 流星群の活動が最も活発な時期。
entries.es: El momento de mayor actividad de la lluvia de meteoros.
entries.pt-BR: O momento de maior atividade da chuva de meteoros.
entries.fr: Le moment où la pluie de météores est la plus active.
entries.de: Der Zeitpunkt, zu dem der Meteorschauer am aktivsten ist.

entries.ja: 何かに気づいたり、それを目にしたりすること。特に、見えにくいものを見つけること。
entries.ko: 무언가를 알아차리거나 보는 것. 특히 눈에 잘 띄지 않는 것을 발견하는 것.
entries.zh-Hans: 注意到或看见某样东西，尤其是不容易看见的东西。
entries.es: Notar o ver algo, especialmente cuando es difícil de ver.
entries.pt-BR: Perceber ou ver algo, especialmente quando é difícil de enxergar.
entries.fr: Remarquer ou voir quelque chose, surtout quand on a du mal à le voir.
entries.de: Etwas bemerken oder sehen, besonders wenn es schwer zu sehen ist.

entries.ja: 何かが移動するときに、そのあとに線のように残る物質。
entries.ko: 무언가가 움직이면서 지나간 자리에 물질이 선 모양으로 남은 것.
entries.zh-Hans: 物体移动时沿途留下的呈线状的物质。
entries.es: Una línea de material que algo deja a su paso.
entries.pt-BR: Uma linha de material que fica para trás quando algo se move.
entries.fr: Une ligne de matière laissée par quelque chose qui se déplace.
entries.de: Eine Linie aus Material, die etwas bei seiner Bewegung hinterlässt.

entries.ja: 細長い線。ここでは、光が作る線のこと。
entries.ko: 길고 가느다란 선들로, 여기서는 빛으로 이루어져 있다.
entries.zh-Hans: 又长又细的线条，这里指光形成的线条。
entries.es: Líneas largas y estrechas, en este caso formadas por luz.
entries.pt-BR: Linhas longas e finas, neste caso formadas por luz.
entries.fr: De longues lignes fines, formées ici par de la lumière.
entries.de: Lange, schmale Linien, die hier aus Licht bestehen.

entries.ja: 双眼鏡や望遠鏡などの道具を使わず、自分の目だけで見ること。
entries.ko: 쌍안경이나 망원경 같은 장비 없이 눈으로 보는 것.
entries.zh-Hans: 不借助双筒望远镜或天文望远镜等设备，只用眼睛看。
entries.es: Usando solo los ojos, sin instrumentos como binoculares o un telescopio.
entries.pt-BR: Usando apenas os olhos, sem equipamentos como binóculos ou telescópio.
entries.fr: En utilisant seulement ses yeux, sans se servir d’instruments comme des jumelles ou un télescope.
entries.de: Nur mit den eigenen Augen, ohne Hilfsmittel wie ein Fernglas oder ein Teleskop.

entries.ja: 明るい場所から暗い場所に移るときなど、変化に慣れること。
entries.ko: 밝은 곳에서 어두운 곳으로 옮겨 갈 때처럼, 어떤 변화에 익숙해지는 것.
entries.zh-Hans: 适应某种变化，比如从明亮的地方进入黑暗的地方。
entries.es: Acostumbrarse a un cambio, como pasar de un lugar iluminado a uno oscuro.
entries.pt-BR: Acostumar-se a uma mudança, como passar de um lugar claro para um escuro.
entries.fr: S’habituer à un changement, comme lorsqu’on passe d’un endroit lumineux à un endroit sombre.
entries.de: Sich an eine Veränderung gewöhnen, etwa wenn man von einem hellen Ort an einen dunklen wechselt.

entries.ja: ある種類の天気になる見込みだと伝える。
entries.zh-Hans: 表示预计会出现某种天气。
entries.es: Indica que se espera un determinado tipo de tiempo.
entries.pt-BR: Indica que são esperadas determinadas condições do tempo.
entries.fr: Indique qu’un certain type de temps est prévu.
entries.de: Gibt an, dass mit einer bestimmten Art von Wetter zu rechnen ist.

entries.ja: 何かが邪魔になって、見ようとしているものが見えなくなること。
entries.ko: 시야를 가려서 누군가가 보려는 것을 볼 수 없게 하는 것.
entries.zh-Hans: 挡住视线，使人看不到想看的东西。
entries.es: Interponerse de modo que alguien no pueda ver lo que está tratando de mirar.
entries.pt-BR: Ficar no caminho e impedir que alguém veja o que está tentando observar.
entries.fr: S’interposer de sorte qu’une personne ne puisse pas voir ce qu’elle essaie de regarder.
entries.de: So im Weg sein, dass jemand nicht sehen kann, was er zu sehen versucht.

entries.ja: 空が陸や海と接しているように見える線よりも低い位置に。
entries.ko: 하늘이 땅이나 바다와 맞닿아 보이는 선보다 낮은 곳에.
entries.zh-Hans: 在天空看起来与陆地或海面相接的那条线下方。
entries.es: Por debajo de la línea donde el cielo parece encontrarse con la tierra o el mar.
entries.pt-BR: Abaixo da linha onde o céu parece encontrar a terra ou o mar.
entries.fr: Plus bas que la ligne où le ciel semble rejoindre la terre ou la mer.
entries.de: Unterhalb der Linie, an der der Himmel das Land oder das Meer zu berühren scheint.
